title: On the Deep Seafloor, a Dead Whale Feeds Hundreds for 50 Years
subject: whale

scenes.text: Deep in the ocean, a dead whale is a miracle. Here is why.
It sinks kilometer by kilometer to the seabed. Scientists call that a whale fall.
Hagfish, sleeper sharks and crabs strip the flesh in months to two years.
Then bone-eating worms called Osedax move in, and can stay on one carcass for up to ten years.
Finally, bacteria break down the bones and make hydrogen sulfide, which feeds clams and tube worms for 10 to 50 years.
One body, hundreds of animals, up to fifty years. That is the miracle.

description:
When a whale dies, the body sinks to the deep seafloor and becomes a whale fall.
One carcass can feed hundreds of marine animals for up to 50 years.
What would you want to see down there?
first_comment: Did you know a dead whale feeds a whole world? Which deep sea mystery should we cover next?
